# Atlas Community Hub Research Brief

This document is entirely synthetic and is included for local testing and demonstrations. Atlas Community Hub is a fictional project; the names, figures, and recommendations below do not describe a real organization or person.

## Executive summary

The fictional Atlas team is evaluating a solar-powered community hub for a six-week pilot. The pilot budget is $48,000, and the team will use a modular battery system to support evening programming.

## Pilot plan

- Pilot duration: six weeks.
- Pilot budget: $48,000.
- Primary success criterion: at least 80% of scheduled evening sessions operate without an unplanned power interruption.
- Secondary success criterion: at least 60% of visitors complete the short feedback survey.

## Risks and mitigations

The main operational risk is battery replacement during periods of heavy use. The mitigation is to keep one charged spare module on site and review battery health at the end of each day.

The team should not treat a successful pilot as proof that the hub can operate indefinitely. A longer trial would still be needed to evaluate seasonal weather, maintenance costs, and equipment replacement intervals.

## Decision rule

At the end of the pilot, proceed to a larger trial only if both primary and secondary success criteria are met and no unresolved safety issue remains. If either metric is below target, document the cause and repeat the pilot after the mitigation is tested.
